walkthroughs.body_html:
Typhoon Haiyan hit the Philippines on 8 November 2013.

Sustained winds of about 315 km/h and a 5 m surge at Tacloban.

Over 6,300 people lost their lives.

Hurricane Sandy hit the US east coast in October 2012.

It killed about 233 people overall but caused $70 billion of damage.

NYC's subway flooded and millions lost power.

Comparison shows the role of development.

The US had stronger forecasting, evacuation and insurance.

The Philippines suffered far more deaths despite a similar storm.

mcqs.q: Why do earthquakes typically cause more deaths in LICs than HICs?
options: LICs often have poorly enforced building codes, weak emergency response, dense informal housing and limited preparedness — not because the earthquakes are stronger.
All earthquakes of magnitude 7 cause the same damage everywhere.
LICs have more earthquake deaths because more earthquakes happen there.
HICs never have earthquake deaths because of advanced technology.

mcqs.q: Why do earthquakes of similar magnitude cause different amounts of damage?
options: Lag time is the delay between thunder and lightning.
All earthquakes of magnitude 7 cause the same damage everywhere.
Bigger magnitude always means more deaths.
Damage depends on depth, distance from population, building quality, ground type (liquefaction risk), time of day, and emergency preparedness — not just magnitude.
